head: c790227e0cda780e6fea9bb03af27948d9e286b9
title: The retry-count delete ignores the method, so it removes reminders of every type, not just SMS.
reason: Only scheduleSMSReminders.ts (lines 184/195) ever increments WorkflowReminder.retryCount, so the unfiltered `retryCount > 1` branch can only match SMS reminders; the failure needs other code that does not exist.

head: c790227e0cda780e6fea9bb03af27948d9e286b9
title: A database write inside the catch block can throw and abort the whole cron run.
reason: The new unguarded `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch (lines 190-197) can throw (P2025 if the reminder was deleted, or a repeated DB error), which escapes the for-loop and aborts the rest of the cron run; before this change the catch only logged.

head: 9fde0e906897cc0f4f71793f647dd629faba3317
title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses bogus computed keys, so sync-mode parsing removes every field except access_token.
reason: `[z.string().toString()]` gives the key "[object Object]", so both computed entries collapse into one optional key. zod's default strip mode then removes every field except access_token, including the expiry.

head: 9fde0e906897cc0f4f71793f647dd629faba3317
title: In sync mode the fetch Response has no `.data`, so Google token refresh crashes.
reason: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, so `res?.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` (line 95) throws. The catch block swallows it and the refresh silently never happens.

head: 9fde0e906897cc0f4f71793f647dd629faba3317
title: Google credential key is overwritten with the SafeParseResult wrapper instead of the token data.
reason: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result `{success, data}`, and line 97–100 stores it as `key`. On the next load, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails, even with sync off.

head: 9fde0e906897cc0f4f71793f647dd629faba3317
title: In sync mode HubSpot treats the raw fetch Response as a token and saves it as the credential key.
reason: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, so `expiresIn` is undefined, `expiryDate` becomes NaN, and the Response object is written to credential.key (line 198).

head: 9fde0e906897cc0f4f71793f647dd629faba3317
title: Salesforce refreshes on every client build, throws on an empty statusText, and never uses the new token.
reason: getClient runs a refresh_token exchange on every construction and still builds the Connection from `credentialKey.access_token` (line 106). The file also never imports prisma (the only match is the call on line 96).

head: 9fde0e906897cc0f4f71793f647dd629faba3317
title: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects the user id.
reason: Line 93 passes `credentialId`, which refreshOAuthTokens sends as `calcomUserId`, while every other integration passes credential.userId.

head: 9fde0e906897cc0f4f71793f647dd629faba3317
title: A placeholder "refresh_token" can overwrite the real stored refresh token.
reason: The Office schema has `refresh_token: z.string().optional()`, so a response without one gets the placeholder "refresh_token". The spread on line 264 then overwrites the real stored refresh token, which the old code kept.

head: 9fde0e906897cc0f4f71793f647dd629faba3317
title: The webhook secret is compared with plain `!==`, which leaks timing.
reason: The plain `!==` comparison on lines 24–29 is real, but a timing attack against a JS string compare over the network is hard to exploit, so it is unclear whether this matters.

head: 9fde0e906897cc0f4f71793f647dd629faba3317
title: The sync request is unauthenticated and its HTTP status is never checked.
reason: The code comment says "Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires", so the self-hoster is meant to add authentication. Office already checks the status through handleErrorsJson.

head: 9fde0e906897cc0f4f71793f647dd629faba3317
title: An invalid Office 365 token response now throws, and the merge can still store the SafeParseResult.
reason: Throwing on an invalid token response instead of saving stale credentials, and losing a console.error, is a behaviour and logging choice rather than a demonstrated failure. The sync-mode schema problem is already covered by finding 0.

head: 9fde0e906897cc0f4f71793f647dd629faba3317
title: Bad bodies and failed decryption surface as unhandled 500s.
reason: A malformed authenticated webhook request returning 500 instead of 400 is error-handling polish, not a defect.

head: 9fde0e906897cc0f4f71793f647dd629faba3317
title: The redirect URI was hardcoded instead of using `appConfig.slug`, which the request does not cover.
reason: The hardcoded "zoho-bigin" matches the app's slug and callback route, so nothing breaks; this is style.

head: 54486a059cd2032042189bb565646ba4e0f6bd61
title: A backup code with any non-empty totpCode logs in without checking the password or the TOTP.
reason: Line 121 skips password verification whenever totpCode is set, and the backup-code branch at 131 never checks TOTP, so email + any totpCode + one backup code yields a session.

head: 54486a059cd2032042189bb565646ba4e0f6bd61
title: Closing the dialog on the backup-codes step leaves 2FA enabled but the UI unaware.
reason: Parent two-factor-auth.tsx onOpenChange only toggles enableModalOpen and never calls utils.viewer.me.invalidate(), so dismissing on the backup-codes step leaves the switch stale and step stuck at DisplayBackupCodes.

head: 54486a059cd2032042189bb565646ba4e0f6bd61
title: First 2FA test never dismisses the new backup-codes screen and relies on an assertion that always passes.
reason: Test-only weakness the author explicitly acknowledged with the FIXME comment at lines 50-51; not a product defect.

head: 54486a059cd2032042189bb565646ba4e0f6bd61
title: A backup code is used up with an unguarded read-then-write, so two parallel logins can both use it.
reason: Lines 139-156 decrypt the earlier-fetched user.backupCodes and write back unconditionally, so concurrent requests with the same code both pass the indexOf check.

head: 54486a059cd2032042189bb565646ba4e0f6bd61
title: Shared PasswordField toggle removed from the keyboard tab order.
reason: Commit 663530d 'fix: make password visible tooltip non-tabbable' shows the tabIndex={-1} change is intentional.

head: 54486a059cd2032042189bb565646ba4e0f6bd61
title: Passing `type="password"` to PasswordField breaks its show/hide toggle.
reason: PasswordField sets type={isPasswordVisible ? 'text' : 'password'} then spreads {...props} after (Input.tsx lines 36-39), so the passed type='password' overrides and the toggle has no effect.

head: 54486a059cd2032042189bb565646ba4e0f6bd61
title: The copied toast shows even when the clipboard write fails.
reason: Every other navigator.clipboard.writeText call in the repo (EventTypeSingleLayout, ApiKeyDialogForm, etc.) is un-awaited with a success toast; this matches project convention and is a minor nit.

head: 820d7fa87e0c824c5dee8082a33efadb1a2566f7
title: `import()` runs as soon as the module loads, so no app loading is deferred.
reason: The old static imports in index.ts loaded all app modules at startup too, so eager `import()` causes no new failure; the finding amounts to 'does not defer as described', and a module failing to load would already have broken startup before.

head: 820d7fa87e0c824c5dee8082a33efadb1a2566f7
title: The async `forEach` callback moves `getCalendar` errors outside the try/catch.
reason: getCalendar is now async (getCalendar.ts line 9) and constructs `new CalendarService(credential)` on line 22, so a constructor error that the try/catch used to catch now rejects inside a `forEach(async …)` callback nobody handles.

head: 820d7fa87e0c824c5dee8082a33efadb1a2566f7
title: The async `forEach` callback moves `getCalendar` errors outside the try/catch.
reason: Same as finding 1: `forEach(async …)` on line 125 drops the promise, so errors from the now-async getCalendar (constructor on getCalendar.ts:22) escape the surrounding try/catch as unhandled rejections.

head: 820d7fa87e0c824c5dee8082a33efadb1a2566f7
title: The async `forEach` callback drops the promises, and rejections go unhandled.
reason: Line 553 `forEach(async …)` drops the promise, so a getCalendar or constructor error that used to propagate and fail the mutation is now an unhandled rejection.

head: 5fd11f9faa79c4aefd39975d1b0e963e5034f793
title: `sed -i ''` only works with BSD/macOS sed and fails on Linux.
reason: Line 68 `sed -i '' -E "s|...|" "$ENV_FILE"`: GNU sed takes `''` as the script and the `s|...|` expression as a file name, so the update fails on Linux, and line 73 still prints success.

head: 5fd11f9faa79c4aefd39975d1b0e963e5034f793
title: The dev:cron runner was swapped from ts-node to tsx, which the request does not cover.
reason: This only says the change is out of scope, and the author made it on purpose in commit a8747ea ("Update dev:cron script to use npx tsx"); no failure is shown.

head: 5fd11f9faa79c4aefd39975d1b0e963e5034f793
title: Existing cache rows get the migration time as `updatedAt`, so old caches look freshly updated.
reason: Commit 5fd11f9 says the author chose `DEFAULT NOW()` on purpose so existing and legacy rows get a valid timestamp.

head: 5fd11f9faa79c4aefd39975d1b0e963e5034f793
title: ENV_FILE is resolved against the current directory, not the script's location.
reason: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` (line 5) is resolved from the current directory, so running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root creates or edits a .env outside the repository.

head: 5fd11f9faa79c4aefd39975d1b0e963e5034f793
title: The cache timestamp is always formatted with the "en-US" locale.
reason: Lines 89-92 hard-code `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, so the date ignores the user's locale even though `useLocale` is already imported.

head: 5fd11f9faa79c4aefd39975d1b0e963e5034f793
title: Failures exit with status 0.
reason: This is a local interactive helper that nothing calls (no CI or script uses it), so `exit 0` in cleanup changes nothing anyone relies on.

head: 5fd11f9faa79c4aefd39975d1b0e963e5034f793
title: Access denial throws a plain Error, which tRPC reports as a 500.
reason: Line 25 throws a plain `Error`, which tRPC reports as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (a 500) instead of NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN when access is denied.

head: 5fd11f9faa79c4aefd39975d1b0e963e5034f793
title: updateMany with empty data may not bump updatedAt, and it adds a write on every cache refresh.
reason: `updateManyByCredentialId` (selectedCalendar.ts:400) passes the empty `{}` straight to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany`; whether Prisma still bumps `@updatedAt` on an empty update depends on the pinned Prisma version, which I did not check.

head: 5fd11f9faa79c4aefd39975d1b0e963e5034f793
title: The database default may not match the Prisma schema, which would cause migration drift.
reason: schema.prisma line 1719 already declares `updatedAt DateTime @default(now()) @updatedAt`, which matches the migration's `DEFAULT NOW()`.

head: ffbaf8c54269df2ce510de91245760fddce09896
title: Second `downsize` definition silently replaces the 5-argument one.
reason: Ruby has no arity overloading; the 4-arg downsize at line 149 replaces the 5-arg one, so resize_emoji.rb:14 `downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` now raises ArgumentError.

head: ffbaf8c54269df2ce510de91245760fddce09896
title: Client size check is now a fixed 10 MB for every upload type.
reason: The fixed `10 * 1024` cap does reject attachments a site allows above 10 MB, but the PR description says it wants a 'consistent 10 MB limit across file types', so this may be intended.

head: ffbaf8c54269df2ce510de91245760fddce09896
title: Hardcoded 10 MB cap ignores the configured size settings.
reason: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` breaks sites configured above 10 MB, but it matches the 10 MB limit the description asks for.

head: ffbaf8c54269df2ce510de91245760fddce09896
title: The downsize loop ignores failures and may leave `tempfile` reading stale content.
reason: Ignoring the return value only wastes a few convert runs before Upload.create_for rejects the oversized file; the stale-file claim depends on how image_optim replaces files and how Tempfile#size reads an open handle, neither of which I could see.

head: ffbaf8c54269df2ce510de91245760fddce09896
title: Animated GIFs are never detected because the tempfile path has no .gif extension.
reason: When the animated path is chosen, line 67 passes "80%" to gifsicle's `--resize-fit #{dimensions}`, which takes a WxH size, so gifsicle fails and animated GIFs are never shrunk.

head: ffbaf8c54269df2ce510de91245760fddce09896
title: The 413 error message always reports 10 MB.
reason: Only the wording of the 413 alert is at issue, and that number matches the 10 MB cap the change sets on purpose.

head: 4f8aed295a29954023b2849c060ef4fb299d1b5d
title: Anonymous visitors can make the forum fetch pages and create a topic for any URL on the embeddable host.
reason: The only throttle is `retrieved_recently?` in lib/topic_retriever.rb, keyed on the exact `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` string, and `invalid_host?` only checks the host, so changing the query string (`?a=1`, `?a=2`) gets past both, and each new URL fetches the page and creates a new topic.

head: 4f8aed295a29954023b2849c060ef4fb299d1b5d
title: Remote and feed HTML is stored as raw_html and served unsanitised on the forum origin.
reason: Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged for raw_html and best.html.erb renders it with `raw post.cooked`; feed content is unescaped and never sanitised, and an anonymous embed_url containing `'` passes the host check and lands unescaped in `href='#{url}'` on line 13, so it can add an event-handler attribute.

head: 4f8aed295a29954023b2849c060ef4fb299d1b5d
title: Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten into broken same-host paths.
reason: `href.start_with?('/')` is true for `//cdn...`, and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, so the result becomes `prefix/cdn.example.com/...`.

head: 4f8aed295a29954023b2849c060ef4fb299d1b5d
title: The Disqus import loses its `--category` option and the original thread dates, and now fetches every thread over HTTP.
reason: The commit deliberately switched the Disqus import to import_remote and dropped the category option; whether losing the dates and category and aborting on a failed fetch is acceptable is a design call that the repository does not settle.

head: 4f8aed295a29954023b2849c060ef4fb299d1b5d
title: Feed items without a `content` element crash the whole poll.
reason: Line 35 calls `i.content.scrub` without a nil check; a SimpleRSS item with only `<description>` has nil content, so the poll raises, and TopicRetriever calls PollFeed inline.

head: 4f8aed295a29954023b2849c060ef4fb299d1b5d
title: An unrelated, already-shipped migration is changed to `force: true`.
reason: A migration runs only once per schema, and `force: true` only matters if the table already exists, so this is not a realistic data-loss path.

head: 4f8aed295a29954023b2849c060ef4fb299d1b5d
title: `Kernel#open` on a configurable URL can run shell commands.
reason: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is Kernel#open with open-uri loaded; a value that is not a URI, such as `|cmd`, falls back to the original Kernel#open and runs a shell command, which turns admin settings access into command execution on the server.

head: 4f8aed295a29954023b2849c060ef4fb299d1b5d
title: The update path crashes when the embed's post no longer exists.
reason: Post uses Trashable's default_scope (lib/trashable.rb:5), so a soft-deleted post makes `embed.post` nil, and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises when the feed content changes.

head: 4f8aed295a29954023b2849c060ef4fb299d1b5d
title: `<%- end if %>` turns the next template output into the condition of the block.
reason: Applying the postfix `if` to the next buffer append only moves where some whitespace is written; the page renders correctly, so there is no failure.

head: 6669a2d94d76eea3b99b8c476d12b1eb66726b07
title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row or the row has a NULL notification level.
reason: Line 105 `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil for a user with no row, and line 107 `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError; `TopicUser.change` (topic_user.rb:77) exists and creates the row.

head: 6669a2d94d76eea3b99b8c476d12b1eb66726b07
title: The shared `unsubscribe_link` string now needs `%{unsubscribe_url}`, which emails other than notifications do not pass.
reason: The only sender with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` is user_notifications.rb:294, which passes `unsubscribe_url` on line 295; the digest uses `unsubscribe_link` only as an argument to its own string, and RejectionMailer forbids the option.

head: 6669a2d94d76eea3b99b8c476d12b1eb66726b07
title: A state-changing GET lowers the level again on every hit, so a reload or link prefetch mutes the topic.
reason: Lines 107-111 step the level down on every GET with no confirmation, so a second visit or reload turns regular into muted.

head: 267d8be1f556ed59639ced396c885bb44586da19
title: `include_website_name` is missing the `?`, so ActiveModel::Serializer never calls it.
reason: Line 153 defines `include_website_name` without the `?`. ActiveModel::Serializer only checks `include_<attr>?`, which is the form the same file uses at line 161 (`include_card_image_badge_id?`), so this filter is never called and `website_name` is always serialized, as null when no website is set.

head: 060cda77729cb1c4a827560e09e89a7b22078ba9
title: totalPages counts one page too many when user_count is an exact multiple of limit.
reason: Line 13 `Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1` gives 2 for 50/50, so `showingLast` stays false on the real last page and `next` loads an empty page at offset=user_count.

head: 060cda77729cb1c4a827560e09e89a7b22078ba9
title: Public group members page now shows only the first 50 members and has no way to page.
reason: group.js now always sends `limit: 50` and the server paginates every group, but group/members.hbs has no page controls, so the public page shows at most 50 members where it used to show all of them.

head: 060cda77729cb1c4a827560e09e89a7b22078ba9
title: Public members endpoint accepts any client-supplied limit/offset with no bounds.
reason: Before this change non-automatic groups returned every member with no limit, and automatic groups already took client limit/offset as-is, so the change does not make bounds handling worse.

head: 060cda77729cb1c4a827560e09e89a7b22078ba9
title: Add-members input is never cleared, so adding twice re-adds existing members.
reason: The migration adds a unique index on group_users [:group_id, :user_id] and `Group#add` just calls `users.push`, so re-submitting the uncleared usernames raises RecordNotUnique (a 500), and `addMembers` has no failure handler.

head: 060cda77729cb1c4a827560e09e89a7b22078ba9
title: Removing a member through `group.users.delete(id)` skips the model's removal logic and errors on non-members.
reason: GroupUser's only callback-like behaviour is `counter_cache: "user_count"`; whether `users.delete(id)` on the through association updates it depends on the Rails version, which I did not check, and non-member ids are not reachable from the UI.

head: 7562f37880367411a62304bcdcdc178bced23906
title: The denial-cache test passes even without the denial cache.
reason: setupService uses an empty fakeStore{} and line 528 handles a nil basicRole without error, so with the cached entry set to `false` (line 982) the store fallback also denies and the test passes without the denial cache.

head: 7562f37880367411a62304bcdcdc178bced23906
title: Denials are cached with no invalidation, so a resource can stay denied after access is granted.
reason: The denial TTL is the same 30s shortCacheTTL that permCache already used, and the finding admits it cannot show that a denied check on the new resource runs before the creator's permission is written; whether the create flow does that could not be confirmed.

head: 7562f37880367411a62304bcdcdc178bced23906
title: An ambiguous denial cache key lets one resource's denial apply to another.
reason: A collision in userPermDenialCacheKey needs two specially chosen UIDs whose underscores line up, and the only effect is a wrongly cached denial for 30s, never a wrongly allowed request — too unlikely and too small for a comment.

head: 1cab4143d443c33079566f6ca36931eb8468159f
title: Queries may be template-interpolated twice, applying ad-hoc filters twice.
reason: Sub-requests keep request.filters/scopedVars ({...request, targets} at querySplitting.ts:174) and go through runQuery -> super.query, where DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185 calls applyTemplateVariables again; addAdHocFilters/addLabelToQuery (modifyQuery.ts:200-211) don't skip filters already present, so the filters are added twice and variables are expanded twice.

head: bbd8c507cdf56f6b884373809e0b24abd4a2353d
title: Device tagging now runs synchronously on every anonymous login, without the old timeout or panic recovery.
reason: Commit 566e0a8 'break auth if limit reached' made TagDevice synchronous on purpose so the limit can fail auth; the DB is only hit on a local-cache miss (impl.go:83-87, a 29-minute cache), so this is an intended trade-off.

head: bbd8c507cdf56f6b884373809e0b24abd4a2353d
title: Separate count and insert steps let concurrent new devices exceed the limit.
reason: CountDevices (database.go:110) and the upsert (line 149) run in separate sessions with no transaction or lock, so concurrent new devices can each see count < limit and all be inserted.

head: bbd8c507cdf56f6b884373809e0b24abd4a2353d
title: The callback rewrites the captured `args` slice, so a retried session sends a corrupted argument list.
reason: WithDbSession retries the callback through retryOnLocks (session.go:83), and line 84 reassigns the captured args, so each retry prepends the query again and Exec gets the wrong arguments.

head: bbd8c507cdf56f6b884373809e0b24abd4a2353d
title: Zero rows affected is treated as 'limit reached', which can deny a device that is already registered.
reason: Grafana's MySQL connection string sets clientFoundRows=true (sqlstore.go:287), so RowsAffected counts matched rows and an unchanged update does not return 0.

head: bbd8c507cdf56f6b884373809e0b24abd4a2353d
title: The store's constructor now needs a raw `int64` limit, which the wire dependency setup cannot supply if it still uses `ProvideAnonDBStore`.
reason: pkg/server/wire.go:374-375 still lists anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore and binds AnonStore; the provider now needs an int64 nobody supplies and is unused, so wire generation fails.

head: e369f24665ec70e1e3700f457d25ef83301d931a
title: Background legacy writes use the request context and get cancelled when the request returns.
reason: Lines 51/110/135/163 build the goroutine context from the request ctx, and the request ctx is cancelled once the handler returns, so the async legacy writes can fail with context canceled; nothing in the repo wraps it with WithoutCancel.

head: e369f24665ec70e1e3700f457d25ef83301d931a
title: A failed storage Create is recorded as a legacy duration.
reason: Line 45 calls recordLegacyDuration when d.Storage.Create fails, so a storage failure is counted in the legacy metric; Delete and DeleteCollection use recordStorageDuration in the same spot.

head: e369f24665ec70e1e3700f457d25ef83301d931a
title: A successful storage Delete records the object name as the metric's kind label.
reason: Line 106 passes `name` as the kind label where every other call passes options.Kind, which mislabels the metric and adds one label value per object name.

head: e369f24665ec70e1e3700f457d25ef83301d931a
title: A failed storage Update is recorded as a legacy duration.
reason: Line 129 records a failed d.Storage.Update with recordLegacyDuration, so the failure goes to the wrong metric.

head: e369f24665ec70e1e3700f457d25ef83301d931a
title: Legacy DeleteCollection timing is recorded as a storage duration.
reason: Line 166 records the timing of d.Legacy.DeleteCollection with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration.

head: e369f24665ec70e1e3700f457d25ef83301d931a
title: Legacy write failures are no longer logged.
reason: This is a missing log line; the failure is still counted through recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...), so no behaviour breaks.

head: e369f24665ec70e1e3700f457d25ef83301d931a
title: Legacy Create reads the same `obj` concurrently with the response path.
reason: The handler returns `created`, not `obj`, so a race needs a storage that mutates the input in place or returns the same pointer, and I could not confirm that from the code shown.

head: e369f24665ec70e1e3700f457d25ef83301d931a
title: Legacy Update re-runs the original objInfo instead of writing the object storage produced.
reason: Line 139 passes the raw objInfo to Legacy.Update, while mode2 (line 298) and the old mode3 code wrapped the storage result in updateWrapper, so legacy recomputes the update and the stores can diverge or conflict.

head: e369f24665ec70e1e3700f457d25ef83301d931a
title: Delete puts the base logger into the context instead of the enriched one.
reason: Line 97 only affects which logger fields go into the context; it is a logging detail, not a functional defect.

head: e369f24665ec70e1e3700f457d25ef83301d931a
title: Delete no longer reaches legacy when unified storage returns NotFound.
reason: Mode 3 treats unified storage as the source of truth (reads come only from Storage), so returning NotFound from storage matches the described design.

head: e369f24665ec70e1e3700f457d25ef83301d931a
title: Mode 3 integration tests may be flaky because legacy writes are asynchronous.
reason: With FlagKubernetesPlaylists enabled, the /api/playlists calls in doPlaylistTests go through the k8s API and the dual writer, and mode 3 serves reads from unified storage, so the tests do not read legacy right after an async write.

head: 3214b188de808fdb0fff335556b686f1b0a63218
title: The new `user != null` check turns off passkeys on the normal login page.
reason: Line 161 adds `&& user != null`, so both callers (lines 115 and 137) now skip fillContextForm on a fresh login with no user, the exact case that used to set up passkeys.

head: 3214b188de808fdb0fff335556b686f1b0a63218
title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called without an argument, but the only version shown takes a `UserModel`.
reason: UsernameForm.java:47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no argument, and the only definition in the package is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) at UsernamePasswordForm.java:160, so it does not compile.

head: 3214b188de808fdb0fff335556b686f1b0a63218
title: During re-authentication the passkey prompt no longer limits which credentials are allowed, so a different user's passkey could be accepted.
reason: WebAuthnAuthenticator.action() lines 201-211 already rejects a user handle that differs from context.getUser() with WEBAUTHN_ERROR_DIFFERENT_USER, so another user's passkey cannot switch the session.

head: 79d11c4890cc4792e3dc3535af59e4e5f7a2739d
title: Removing the multiple-provider error lets a FIPS setup silently run on a non-FIPS provider.
reason: Replacing the multiple-provider error with selection by order() is the approach the PR description explicitly chooses (approach 2 from #32962), so this is a deliberate design choice, not a defect.

head: 79d11c4890cc4792e3dc3535af59e4e5f7a2739d
title: Adding `order()` as an abstract method breaks every existing CryptoProvider implementation.
reason: A repo-wide search shows the only CryptoProvider implementations (AuthzClient, Default, WildFlyElytron and FIPS1402, with Fips1402Strict inheriting) all define order(), so nothing in the repository breaks.

head: 79d11c4890cc4792e3dc3535af59e4e5f7a2739d
title: Two ASN.1 encoders are built and thrown away.
reason: Lines 114-115 only create two throwaway encodings; the returned value is unaffected, so this is a negligible allocation and style issue, not a defect.

head: 79d11c4890cc4792e3dc3535af59e4e5f7a2739d
title: The ES384 and ES512 tests sign with a P-256 key, so they never test those curves' sizes.
reason: This asks for more test coverage; the round-trip assertion in ECDSAAlgorithmTest is still correct with the default-curve key from line 42, so there is no defect.

head: 62bf98939eda58f0d0a1a41a58aa6d4ecdc24dba
title: Exit code 4 changes meaning from "recreate required" to "feature disabled".
reason: No operator code reads the check exit code (no exitCode references in operator/src/main), and the renumbering (3 = recreate, 4 = rolling-updates disabled) is intended and documented in update-compatibility.adoc lines 128-134 for this preview tool.

head: 02f48f776f43734d1ac8914d3ad6a7115acdcb33
title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with an Italian sentence.
reason: Line 101 of the account messages_lt.properties now reads 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian text in the Lithuanian bundle.

head: 02f48f776f43734d1ac8914d3ad6a7115acdcb33
title: Simplified Chinese bundle now has a Traditional Chinese string.
reason: Line 112 of messages_zh_CN.properties uses Traditional characters (手機/安裝/應用程式) in the Simplified Chinese bundle, while the lines around it are Simplified.

head: 02f48f776f43734d1ac8914d3ad6a7115acdcb33
title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with an Italian sentence.
reason: Line 71 of the login messages_lt.properties sets loginTotpStep1 to the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'.

head: 02f48f776f43734d1ac8914d3ad6a7115acdcb33
title: Account UI message switched from i18next `{{0}}` placeholders to MessageFormat syntax.
reason: ThemeResource.getLocalizationTexts sends raw message values, account-ui i18n.ts uses default i18next {{}} interpolation with no ICU plugin, and ui-shared user-profile/utils.ts formats the error client-side with t(), so '{0}' and '{2,choice,...}' would show up literally.

head: 02f48f776f43734d1ac8914d3ad6a7115acdcb33
title: Admin UI message switched from i18next `{{0}}` placeholders to MessageFormat syntax.
reason: admin-ui i18n.ts uses plain i18next with default {{}} interpolation, loads raw values from ThemeResource without conversion, and formats user-profile errors client-side via ui-shared utils.ts, so the MessageFormat syntax would not be filled in.

head: ce2dcc537b4b1f98a335e88cfe8e0b804483252a
title: A credential from user storage can now be passed to `removeStoredCredentialById`, which only works on the local store.
reason: getCredential now returns the federated credential first, and line 86 passes its id to removeStoredCredentialById, which for a federated user calls JpaUserFederatedStorageProvider.removeStoredCredential; its em.find(..., id) (line 602) fails on a null id and finds nothing for a provider-owned id, and the test provider's createFromValues model sets no id.

head: ce2dcc537b4b1f98a335e88cfe8e0b804483252a
title: `getCredentials` throws a NullPointerException when the user is not in the provider's map.
reason: This is a null check in a test-only provider; getCredentials is only called for users this provider returned, which are always in its users map, so it is not a real defect.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: OptimizedCursorPaginator applies numeric math to the `datetime` key, so the optimized path crashes.
reason: Line 840 calls math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, 'datetime') (a datetime, since the endpoint uses order_by='-datetime'), which raises TypeError on any non-empty page, unlike DateTimePaginator's strftime conversion.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: Negative offsets from the client are passed straight into a Django queryset slice, which raises an error.
reason: Cursor.from_string/__init__ accept negative offsets unchecked (cursors.py:28,59), Django querysets reject negative slicing with ValueError, and base.py paginate only catches BadPaginationError (line 540), so the request returns a 500.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: The admin check is wrong, and it runs on every request even when the optimized path is not requested.
reason: RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None = None` (model.py:346) and line 71 dereferences it on every request before use_optimized is checked, so a non-superuser caller without a membership gets an AttributeError.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: The shared BasePaginator still passes negative offsets through for prev cursors.
reason: Before this change BasePaginator sliced `queryset[offset:stop]` with the raw offset in both directions, so negative prev offsets already failed; the change only adds clamping for the non-prev case and does not make anything worse.

head: bb75657fc8f13923c1d7983f422290908a1e7310
title: Accessing `metadata["sender"]["login"]` directly crashes when the integration has no sender
reason: build_integration adds sender only when state.get("sender") is set (line 376), and github/installation.py:44 already guards `"sender" not in integration.metadata`, so the unguarded metadata["sender"]["login"] at line 503 can raise KeyError.

head: bb75657fc8f13923c1d7983f422290908a1e7310
title: `test_installation_not_found` no longer tests the 404 path
reason: In the rewritten test the first request has no state and only redirects to OAuth authorize; the second sends state 'ddd023…', which fails the signature check at line 412 before build_integration's 404 branch, so the 404 path is no longer covered.

head: bb75657fc8f13923c1d7983f422290908a1e7310
title: Network and API failures in the token exchange and user lookup cause a 500
reason: get_user_info calls resp.raise_for_status() (provider.py:16) and safe_urlopen at line 423 is outside the try, so network or API errors escape the view as a 500 instead of the error page.

head: bb75657fc8f13923c1d7983f422290908a1e7310
title: OAuth authorize URL query parameters are not URL-encoded
reason: redirect_uri is absolute_uri(reverse('sentry-extension-setup')), a fixed path with no ?, & or #, and the other values are a client id and a hex signature, so the unescaped query does not break in practice.

head: 6ad6fe3899f630ccf922ce7ac681147dc7987435
title: upsampled_count() counts events with no sample_weight as 0.
reason: Lines 1046-1050 use a bare sum(sample_weight). Nothing in this repo sets sample_weight; event_manager.py:776-787 only sets sample_rate when a valid client_sample_rate is present. The commit says it removed the null checks, so events with no weight count as 0.

head: 6ad6fe3899f630ccf922ce7ac681147dc7987435
title: An unrelated submodule gitlink `sentry-repo` was committed.
reason: The diff adds a gitlink, sentry-repo, pointing at an unrelated otlp commit (a5d29095). It has nothing to do with the upsampling feature and is plainly an accidental nested checkout.

head: 6ad6fe3899f630ccf922ce7ac681147dc7987435
title: The substring check treats negated or mixed queries as error-only.
reason: Line 137 is a plain substring test, `"event.type:error" in query`, which also matches `!event.type:error` and queries that OR in other event types, so count() gets upsampled for non-error-only discover queries.

head: 6ad6fe3899f630ccf922ce7ac681147dc7987435
title: The eligibility check uses the outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`.
reason: The split paths at lines 355-407 run only when metrics_enhanced is true, so the outer dataset is a metrics dataset and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns False. The transform therefore never runs against transactions.

head: 6ad6fe3899f630ccf922ce7ac681147dc7987435
title: Allowlist changes can take up to 60 seconds to apply, and nothing invalidates the cache.
reason: The 60-second cache is intentional: the commit message and the docstring (lines 23-25) say allowlist changes are infrequent and eventual consistency is acceptable.

head: 3162ad68a5c87666788b27a44eb31235025091a9
title: A hung flusher process is no longer killed before its replacement starts.
reason: Line 254 checks `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, but CPython's `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so the check is always False for spawn processes and the hung process is never killed before line 259 starts its replacement.

head: 3162ad68a5c87666788b27a44eb31235025091a9
title: The added `time.sleep(0.1)` does nothing because the test replaces `time.sleep` with a no-op.
reason: Line 15 replaces `time.sleep` on the `time` module with a no-op, so the new `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 returns immediately, and `join()` (line 331) sets `stopped` right away, so the flusher thread can still exit before it flushes.

head: 3162ad68a5c87666788b27a44eb31235025091a9
title: The `wait_produce` metric uses the tag key `shards`; the other new metrics use `shard`.
reason: Line 199 tags `wait_produce` with `shards`, while lines 185 and 195 tag the other new metrics with `shard`, so a query that filters on `shard` will miss this metric.

head: 8422030ef456e3a898415e96475b4d8ddfc7640f
title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract, so building it raises TypeError.
reason: StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (detector.py:142-170), MetricAlertDetectorHandler only has `pass`, and MetricAlertFire.detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler is instantiated with no guard at models/detector.py:86, so a metric_alert_fire detector raises TypeError.

head: 8422030ef456e3a898415e96475b4d8ddfc7640f
title: The expected occurrence is built for group key "val1", but the test evaluates "group_key".
reason: IssueOccurrence.__eq__ compares only `id` (issue_occurrence.py:181-184), and build_mock_occurrence_and_event always uses the same fixed id, so the different fingerprint does not make the comparison fail.
